claims.text: The feedstock consists of spherical, atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder with a uniform particle-size distribution.
A primary laser operating at approximately 150 W and 600 mm/s is suitable for depositing the AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
An approximately 50 W secondary laser can provide effective immediate post-deposition annealing.
A secondary-laser delay of approximately 0.5 s will provide controlled cooling without overheating.
The proposed protocol is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi components with characteristic dimensions of approximately 5 mm.
The components should be processed in an inert argon atmosphere.
Substrate preheating to approximately 300°C is part of the applicable processing window.
The timed secondary laser pass moderates the thermal environment and mitigates extreme thermal gradients.
The moderated thermal environment permits diffusion-driven grain coalescence.
The timed annealing pass promotes controlled phase transitions.
The dual-laser process produces a refined microstructure characterized by low-angle grain boundaries.
The dual-laser process enhances phase homogeneity.
The dual-laser process reduces microstructural defect density.
Mitigation of thermal gradients and rapid-cooling effects relieves residual stress.
Relative to primary-laser-only processing, the dual-laser protocol will reduce XRD-measured residual stress by approximately 30%.
The dual-laser protocol will improve ductility relative to conventional high-energy deposition.
The dual-laser protocol will produce a more uniform microhardness profile than conventional high-energy deposition.
In situ secondary-laser annealing eliminates the need for a separate post-build heat treatment.
Eliminating separate post-build heat treatment simplifies the overall manufacturing process.
Inadequate synchronization can cause overheating, improper melt-pool dynamics, or adverse microstructural degradation.
